LEARNING PATH LESSON · SPORTS & MOVEMENT · AGES 4–5 YEARS

Golf — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches golf as the wall’s whisper: where hockey pushes and baseball whips, golf swings SLOW — and counts every tap on the way to the hole.

What is this?

Golf is a target game on a very big course: swing the club, send the small ball toward the hole, and count how many strokes it takes. Fewest taps wins — and slow swings beat strong ones every time.

What does it mean?

Golf is the control sport. Every other card rewards force; golf rewards restraint — the smoother the swing, the straighter the ball. For a four-year-old that is a brand-new idea: sometimes the body wins by slowing down.

What does the child need to know?

Your child needs three golf ideas: hands hold the club like two friends sharing one handle; the swing is a pendulum — back slow, through slower; and every tap is a COUNT — the counting is not extra, it is the game.

Why this matters

Aiming small and swinging slow grows the precision end of fundamental movement skills — the twin of the big-power skills every other ball game drills. Golf is where the body learns whisper control.

What it teaches

Pendulum swinging (pendulum rhythm is a timing skill all its own), small-target aiming, stroke counting — early maths on the fairway — and the patience of trying again calmly.

Words to learn

golfclubswingputtholestrokecount

Say this to your child

“"Golf is the whisper game! Hold the club like two friends sharing one umbrella. Swing slow — back like a clock, through like a clock, whoooosh. The tiny ball rolls and rolls… and we count every tap: one, two, THREE — in the hole! Fewest taps wins, and slow is the secret."”

Step by step

  1. Show the card: "This is golf — the slow-swing counting game."
  2. The grip: both hands together on the handle, thumbs down the middle — two friends sharing an umbrella.
  3. The pendulum: swing back like a clock hand… and through like a clock hand — smooth, no chopping. Whoooosh, not WHACK.
  4. Putt first: the tiny swing on the carpet, ball rolling to a cup. Count every tap out loud: one… two… three — in the cup!
  5. Play carpet golf below and close: "slow swing, small ball, keep counting."

Look closer at the picture

On this card the word "golf" stands at the top in big letters with the game’s scene below — the club, the small white ball and the green exactly as the game looks on the course.

Ask your child

"Fast swing or slow swing?" "What do we count?" "How do our hands hold the club?"

What your child can say or do

Your child might say: "Whoosh — slow like a clock!" "Three taps and I sank it!" or the golfer’s whisper: "Gentle… gentle… in!"

Out in the real world

Golf lives at courses, driving ranges and mini-golf parks — the mini-putt course is a child’s paradise built exactly on today’s skill. Walk one together and count strokes per hole like the pros.

Try it together

Carpet Golf: a bucket or cup at one end of the carpet, a spoon-club, a pom-pom ball. Stroke one: tap. Stroke two: tap. Sink it in three — par for the living room! Lay a "course" of three cups with sofa-cushion hazards between. The scorecard can be drawn; the counting must be loud.

Understanding check

Ask: "Whack or whoosh? What do we count after every tap? What wins the game?" Whoosh, the strokes, fewest taps — three answers and the whisper game is on.

Parent tips

Make the child the scoreboard — counting strokes is maths practice smuggled into sport. And if the swing keeps chopping, hold a balloon above the clubhead: a swing that pops it is chopping; a swing that never touches is a true pendulum.

This lesson pairs with the Golf flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Sports & Movement (Class 37).
